title: Applied AI Engineer at Bjak
text:
BJAK

Applied AI Engineer

This role focuses on building practical AI agents, workflows, and automations to improve financial products and operational efficiency. You will work closely with product and engineering teams to deploy reliable AI solutions that handle real-world constraints like latency, security, and compliance. The position requires hands-on engineering experience with LLMs, RAG systems, and production-grade software development. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle of AI features, from identifying opportunities to maintaining them in production.

Responsibilities
Build AI agents, workflows, tools, and automations to solve customer and operational problems.
Apply LLMs, retrieval, tool calling, and guardrails to practical financial workflows.
Create AI-assisted experiences for onboarding, KYC, risk review, and CRM.
Collaborate with product and engineering teams to identify and build high-impact features.
Design systems with a focus on accuracy, latency, cost, security, and compliance.
Skills & Requirements
Required Skills:
Python
TypeScript
JavaScript
LLM application development
RAG systems
AI agent design
Production-grade software engineering
Nice-to-Have Skills:
Fintech experience
Banking domain knowledge
Support automation
Fraud detection
KYC/Risk management
About the Company

Bjak is a leading Southeast Asian insurance and financial platform founded in 2019 with a mission to help people plan, save, and grow their money. The company operates globally with a diverse team and is currently expanding its services to include broader financial applications.

Editorial Analysis

The Job in a Nutshell:

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on deploying production-ready AI agents to solve real-world fintech challenges.

What You'll Actually Do:

You will spend your time designing and implementing AI workflows, integrating LLMs into existing financial products, and ensuring the reliability of these systems through rigorous testing and evaluation.

Positive Indicators:

The company emphasizes a fast-paced, builder-centric culture with a clear focus on shipping tangible products rather than just research, which is ideal for engineers who enjoy seeing their code in production.

Considerations:

This role requires a high degree of ownership and accountability for production systems, meaning you must be comfortable with the pressures of reliability, security, and compliance in a financial context.

Written by Surely Remote
Growth Opportunities

Skills You'll Develop:

You will gain deep expertise in AI-native architecture, production-level LLM deployment, financial system automation, and cross-functional product development.

Where This Could Lead:

Success in this role could lead to senior engineering positions, AI architecture roles, or leadership opportunities within Bjak's expanding financial technology ecosystem.

Career Assets You'll Build:

Building and scaling AI-native financial products provides a strong portfolio piece that demonstrates your ability to handle complex, high-stakes technical challenges.

Written by Surely Remote
Application Guide

Optimize Your Resume:

Highlight your experience with LLMs, RAG, Python, TypeScript, and specific examples of AI systems you have deployed to production.

How to Stand Out:

Focus your application on concrete examples of how you have built and scaled systems. During the interview, demonstrate your understanding of the trade-offs between AI performance, latency, and cost, as the company values practical, reliable engineering over theoretical research.

sections.heading: Our Commitment to Your Safety
sections.text: We are committed to a scam-free experience through rigorous vetting. This guide helps you recognize common online job scams, keeping your search safe on any platform.

sections.heading: Empowering Your Search: Know the Signs
sections.text:
• ×
 
 Requests for Financial Account Setup.
 Employers will NEVER ask you to set up a personal payment account (like Stripe) or open an account with a specific online bank using a link they provide. This is a common tactic for fake check and advance-fee scams.
• ×
 
 Impersonation of Real Companies.
 Scammers use names of legitimate companies to appear credible. Be suspicious if the hiring process is too fast, involves few interviews, and the salary seems unusually high.
• ×
 
 Phishing Links for "Banks" or "Onboarding".
 Scammers create fake websites that look real. NEVER click a link from an email to open a bank account. Always check URLs carefully and type official company/bank websites directly into your browser.
• ×
 
 Requests for Payment.
 You should never have to pay for training, equipment, or background checks. Any request for you to send money, buy gift cards, or transfer funds is a scam.
• ×
 
 Unprofessional Communication.
 Be cautious of emails with poor grammar, spelling mistakes, or messages sent from personal email addresses (e.g., @gmail.com) instead of a corporate domain.

sections.heading: Your Safety Checklist:
sections.text:
• ✓
 
 Verify the Offer with the REAL Company.
 If you get an offer, find the company's official website via a search engine. Contact them through their official phone number or careers page to confirm the job opening and your offer are real.
• ✓
 
 Never Share Sensitive Personal Information Early.
 Do not provide bank details, social security numbers, or ID copies until you have independently verified the company and signed a formal employment contract.

sections.heading: A Partnership in Safety
sections.text: Our top priority is your safety, and we work tirelessly to prevent fraudulent listings. While we vet every post, we also believe in empowering you. We encourage you to use these tips to conduct your own verification before sharing sensitive information. Please understand that our platform is a meeting place, and while we are your partners in a safe search, we cannot be held liable for the conduct of third parties.
